article_notes: Zagreb university clinic, 40 dogs with B. canis canis (smear + PCR in all), 30 healthy controls. Groups: uncomplicated (29), one complication (6), MODS (5); 4 MODS dogs died. Admission samples (day of admission); timing relative to imidocarb not stated explicitly. Table 5 superscripts also compare non-anaemic vs mild/moderate anaemia; only the moderate vs mild comparison (stated in text) was extracted as S6, the anaemic vs non-anaemic split is S5. Table 6 correlations of biomarkers with urea, creatinine, bilirubin, ALT, AP and CPK are marker-marker correlations and were not extracted. Haematology and biochemistry by group are only in Additional file 1 (not in text).

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs uncomplicated babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with MODS (two or more organ dysfunctions by the Table 1 criteria: creatinine >180 umol/L, dyspnoea/pulmonary oedema, ALT/AP/bilirubin thresholds, CPK >600 U/L, modified Glasgow coma scale <9) vs dogs with none of the listed complications. Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
severity_definitions.quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.
severity_definitions.definition_source: author-defined (Table 1 criteria; modified Glasgow coma scale from Welzl et al.)

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs one complication
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with MODS vs dogs with a single organ dysfunction (Table 1 criteria). Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
severity_definitions.quote: In dogs with complicated babesiosis, 6 (54.55%) had single organ dysfunction and 5 (45.45%) dogs had MODS.

severity_definitions.label: one complication vs uncomplicated babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with exactly one organ dysfunction by the Table 1 criteria vs dogs with none. Pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests.
severity_definitions.quote: Uncomplicated babesiosis was diagnosed in 29 (72.5%) and complicated babesiosis in the remaining 11 dogs (27.5%).

severity_definitions.label: lethal outcome vs survival
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs that died despite treatment (all had MODS) vs survivors; related to admission biomarkers by Kendall Tau-b correlation. Whether any death was euthanasia and the follow-up horizon are not stated.
severity_definitions.quote: Treatment was successful in all dogs without development of any complications as well as in 7 cases of complicated babesiosis, while 4 dogs with MODS died despite treatment (mortality rate 10%).

severity_definitions.label: anaemic vs non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemia by haematocrit: non-anaemic HCT >37% vs anaemic (HCT <=37%: mild 30-37%, moderate 18-29%, severe <18%).
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: moderately vs mildly anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Moderately anaemic (HCT 18-29%) vs mildly anaemic (HCT 30-37%). The one severely anaemic dog was not analysed.
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: haematocrit (continuous) in infected dogs
severity_definitions.definition: Degree of anaemia as continuous HCT (%) in the 40 infected dogs; Spearman rank correlation with each biomarker. Lower HCT = more severe anaemia.
severity_definitions.quote: Also, there was a significant positive correlation of HCT with GPx and SOD, whereas significant negative correlation of HCT with MDA (Table 6).
